case.case_title: Channa Pieris and Others v. Attorney-General and Others (Ratawesi Peramuna Case)
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1994] 1 Sri LR.

clause.text: No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners were subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment in violation of Article 11 of the Constitution during their arrest and detention.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that their fundamental rights under Article 11 were violated by being subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment during arrest and detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied any violation of Article 11, asserting that no such treatment occurred.
key_facts: Petitioners were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to overthrow the government.
Petitioners were detained under Emergency Regulations.
No evidence was presented to prove torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment.
The court required a high degree of certainty to establish violation of Article 11.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 11 prohibits torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, which may be physical or psychological. The court emphasized that a high degree of certainty is required to prove such violations on a balance of probabilities.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found no evidence or credible submissions to establish that the petitioners were subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment during their arrest or detention.
principles_established: Article 11 protects against torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
Such violations require a high degree of proof.
Absence of evidence means no violation can be declared.

outcome.holding: There was no violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed by Article 11 of the Constitution.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 11 was directly engaged as the petitioners alleged torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment during arrest and detention, but the court found no evidence to support such claims, making the clause central to the court's reasoning and outcome.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court stated that no violation of Article 11 was found as there was no evidence or submissions proving torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
